summary: Weijue Shi (1928–2016) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Lingshuan, Linyuan (~1963), and Lingyuan (~1963–1970). He founded Lin Quan Temple in 1987, Chung Tai Shan, and the Chung Tai Buddhist Institute in 1993.
Weirong Shen (born 1962) specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held teaching posts at The University of Hong Kong and Renmin University of China (~2006).
Weiru Guan is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Wen-ling Jane specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and teacher Geshe Lozang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Hamburg, and Peking University (PhD), and served as a visiting assistant professor at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Stanford University (-1998) and held posts at Barnard College (attested 2008) and the University of Calgary (associate professor, attested 2018).

Wendy Doniger (born 1940) specializes in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She completed degrees at Radcliffe, Harvard (PhD under Daniel H. H. Ingalls), and Oxford (D.Phil. under Robert Charles Zaehner), later serving at the University of Chicago from 1978.

Wenjie Duan (1917–2011) worked in Buddhist studies and archaeology, studying at Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and Central Academy of Fine Arts. He held several leadership roles at the Dunhuang Academy from 1946, serving as director in 1991.

Wenjie Qin specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard University, studying under doctoral supervisor Tu Weiming as well as Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.

Werner Abraham (1936–2024) was a linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna. He held positions at the University of Illinois (~1966–1967), Tübingen (1970–1971), and a professorship at the University of Groningen from 1971.

Werner Sundermann (1935–2012) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1967–1970), the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1970–1992), and the Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).

Wes Borton specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at East Carolina University, where he was taught by Derek F. Maher, and later studied at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. After earning his BA at International Christian University and PhD at Harvard (~1968–1975), he taught at UIUC (~1976–1977) and the University of California, Davis (~1977–2003).

Whitney Cox works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Virginia and the University of Chicago (~1999–2006) under Sheldon Pollock, and held an attested post at the University of Chicago in 2003.

Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne (1928–1986) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at the University of Ceylon and SOAS University of London (PhD ~1954–1956), he held academic and dean posts at the University of Ceylon, Peradeniya, and Kelaniya.
Wilburn Hansen works in religious studies and Japanology. He completed a master's program at the University of Colorado and studied at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith (1916–2000) was a religious studies scholar educated at Toronto, Cambridge, and Princeton (PhD). He held posts at Forman Christian College, McGill University, Dalhousie University, Harvard University (1964–1973; 1978–1985), and Trinity College, Toronto.

Wilfrid Sellars (1912–1989) was a philosopher educated at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He taught at the University of Iowa (1938–1946), University of Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale (1958–1963), and held a professorship at the University of Pittsburgh (1963–1989).

Wilhelm Deecke (1831–1897) worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Leipzig (Dr. phil. 1848–1849) and Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as director or administrator at Ernestinenschule, Gymnasium Jean Sturm, Gymnasium Buchsweiler, and Lycée de Mulhouse.

Wilhelm Dilthey (1833–1911) was a philosopher who studied at Heidelberg and Berlin. He held posts at the University of Basel (~1866–1868), Kiel University (~1868–1871), the University of Breslau (~1871–1882), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1882–1905).
